about: Retrieval evaluation. `expect.passages` lists the passages that must be found (order ignored), each identified by a distinctive substring rather than a heading path so re-chunking does not break the set. `expect.must_contain` lists fact groups the answer needs, each group satisfied by any alternative. Unanswerable cases have no passages and must_refuse instead. See retrieval_scoring.py.

cases.question: Why is the eval suite not run in CI?

passages.contains: a GitHub runner has no model and no way to reach yours

cases.note: Stated in one place under an obvious heading.

cases.question: What port does the Postgres container listen on?
cases.note: A single number, hard to paraphrase away.

cases.question: Which embedding model does the document index use?
cases.note: Named exactly once in a setup block.

cases.question: When does the chat endpoint send the prompt event?
cases.note: A sentence in a table cell.

cases.question: What does the classify endpoint return for blank input?

passages.contains: before any model call is spent

cases.note: Status codes are unambiguous to score.

cases.question: Which origins is the API's CORS configured to allow?
cases.note: Answer is a rule rather than a value.

cases.question: What does a finish reason of length mean?
cases.note: Stemmed alternative so 'truncated'/'truncation' both count.

cases.question: What happens to the index when a documentation file is deleted?

passages.contains: prunes documents no longer on disk

cases.note: Behaviour, not a value.

cases.question: Can I point this at OpenAI or Anthropic instead of running locally?
cases.note: The docs say 'hosted provider'; the question names vendors that appear nowhere in the corpus.

cases.question: If I undo an edit to a prompt, does it go back to its old name?

passages.contains: editing a prompt cannot silently keep its old id

cases.note: The docs say 'identity' and 'digest'; the question says 'name' and 'undo'.

cases.question: The page will not load results in my browser. What would cause that?
cases.note: The word CORS never appears in the question.

cases.question: What stops the model making up a category that is not allowed?
cases.note: Docs say 'decoding grammar' and 'enum'; the question says 'making up'.

cases.question: How do I know two sets of numbers were measured the same way?
cases.note: Docs say 'comparable' and 'scorer_digest'; the question avoids both.

cases.question: Which number tells me how long before the user sees anything?
cases.note: Docs say 'time to first token'; the question describes it instead.

cases.question: Can I try the eval on part of the set without it counting?
cases.note: Docs say 'subset run' and '--group'; the question says 'part of the set'.

cases.question: What do I need installed before anything will run?

passages.contains: Ollama, running, with the model pulled

cases.note: Prerequisites are stated in both READMEs, neither complete alone.

cases.question: Where do prompts live and how are they identified?
cases.note: Location in one document, identity scheme in another.

cases.question: What does CI check and what does it deliberately not check?

passages.contains: a GitHub runner has no model and no way to reach yours

cases.note: The positive and negative halves sit in different documents.

cases.question: What are the parts of this project and what does each one do?
cases.note: Both documents carry a layout table; either alone is partial.

cases.question: What is in a trace and where can I see it?
cases.note: Contents documented in one place, location in another.

cases.question: Why are there two env files and which one does the front end read?

passages.contains: Next.js only reads `.env*` from its own project directory

cases.note: Stated from two angles in two documents.

cases.question: What is the maximum upload size the API accepts?
cases.note: Plausible-sounding API question with no answer in the docs. No forbidden list: every candidate value also appears in the question, so refusal detection alone carries this case.

cases.question: What licence is this project released under?
cases.note: The corpus never states a licence. A named licence here is invention.

cases.question: Who maintains this project and how do I contact them?
cases.note: No ownership information exists in the corpus.

cases.question: How much does it cost per month to run this in production?
cases.note: Cost is discussed only as 'no bill' for local use; a figure would be invented.

cases.question: Which version of Redis does the cache use?
cases.note: There is no Redis and no cache. A false premise the answer must not accept.

cases.question: What is the uptime SLA for the classification endpoint?
cases.note: Another false premise dressed in plausible operational language.

cases.question: How do I reset my password?
cases.note: There are no accounts. The word 'password' appears in the corpus only as a classifier example, which is exactly the vaguely-nearby text refusal must resist.

cases.question: What is the capital of France?
cases.note: Something the model certainly knows but the documentation does not contain.

cases.question: Name one sea.
cases.note: The measured worst case: scores ~0.47 yet retrieval still returns four passages, and the corpus contains the word 'sea' in chat examples.

cases.question: How many requests per minute can I send before being rate limited?
cases.note: Rate limiting is named as out of scope elsewhere, so nearby text exists without an answer. No forbidden list: every candidate value also appears in the question, so refusal detection alone carries this case.
